verdicts.trueWording: Nightflyers ly-adverbs 1.3; A Dance With Dragons 0.4
verdicts.note: Row 20451 of the raw CSV contains the quoted string verbatim as a substring (line begins '20451,'). ly-adverbs column = 1.3; genre list begins ['Science Fiction','Short Stories',...] so 'science-fiction collection' holds. Same file, row 20474, gives A Dance With Dragons ly-adverbs 0.4, so 1.3 is 3.25x - 'more than three times' is exact. Only nuance: the CSV prints bare numbers with no % sign; the percentage unit is prosecraft's convention, not stated on this page.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'both far from the Westeros novels' figures' fails for vividness: the same file lists Fire and Blood (row 21259) at vividness 44.0, closer to Joker Moon's 46.89 than to the ASOIAF novels' 62.65-69.08
verdicts.trueWording: Joker Moon 46.89 vividness, 1.28 ly-adverbs, credited G.R.R. Martin
verdicts.note: Quoted row appears verbatim as a substring of line 20830 ('20828,Joker Moon,George R. R. Martin,171682.0,46.89,8.21,3.22,1.28,1.94,...'). Author field is 'George R. R. Martin' so 'credited to Martin in the dataset' is exact. The ly-adverb limb is strongly supported: 1.28 against A Game of Thrones 0.77, A Clash of Kings 0.68, A Storm of Swords 0.6, A Feast for Crows 0.47, A Dance With Dragons 0.4. The vividness limb holds only if 'the Westeros novels' means the five main-series books; the same page's Fire and Blood row (vividness 44.0) sits nearer Joker Moon's 46.89 than any ASOIAF novel does, so the 'both' is not safe as written.

verdicts.trueWording: 22,449 data rows; six metric columns, none blank
verdicts.note: Parsed the raw CSV: 22,450 lines = 1 header + 22,449 data rows, index column running 0..22448. The quoted header string appears verbatim as a substring of the header line, which is ',title,author,total words,vividness,passive voice,all adverbs,ly-adverbs,non-ly-adverbs,genre,year' - i.e. an unnamed index column precedes it and genre/year follow, but the claim does not say 'only these'. 'each with' checks out: zero blank or NaN values across all six metric columns. Provenance limb ('scraped prosecraft dataset') is not attested on this page itself but is attested in the same repo's raw notebook 0_1_importing_data.ipynb, which I fetched (see index 987). One near-duplicate exists (Dead Man's Hand at rows 21892 and 22190, differing only by curly vs straight apostrophe), so 22,449 is the row count rather than 22,449 wholly distinct works.

verdicts.trueWording: 'My first goal was to obtain a list of books from prosecraft.io'
verdicts.note: Parsed the raw .ipynb JSON: cell 0, the first markdown cell, reads '## Getting the book list\nMy first goal was to obtain a list of books from prosecraft.io. To see what I had to work with, I chose the 50th percentile and checked what the HTML looked like.' - the quote is word for word. The scraping-mechanism limb is supported by cells 1-8: requests + BeautifulSoup against URL = 'http://prosecraft.io/analysis/word-count/percentile/', then the book list pulled out of a 'directory' variable in the first script tag. Nuance, not an unsupported limb: it was one word-count percentile URL, not a sweep of several pages - the single page's embedded script already held the whole directory (cell 12: 'all 24,997 books contained in Prosecraft's database').
